context.intention: I maintain a consistent workout routine.
context.actualStartingPoint: I exercise sporadically. I can use three 30-minute slots each week for bodyweight exercise at home.
context.destinationDescription: I maintain a consistent workout routine.

analysis.startingPointSummary: The person currently exercises sporadically and has three 30-minute home bodyweight slots each week available.
assumptions: A consistent workout routine can be evidenced by repeatable weekly behavior rather than a specific fitness metric.
Bodyweight training at home is a sufficient format for the route.
The goal is to move from sporadic exercise to a stable routine without adding new equipment or time commitments.

routeDesign.complexityReason: This is a behavior-change goal with known time availability and no extra resource barriers. The main achievements are a workable first week, then a routine that survives a disrupted week, then a self-directed rhythm.
routeDesign.countReason: Three waypoints are enough to capture the distinct states: first repeatable week, resilience through disruption, and sustained consistency. More rows would repeat the same habit state rather than add new achievements.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: At least one full week of three home bodyweight workouts is completed using the available 30-minute slots.

waypoints.title: Complete one full workout week
waypoints.rationale: This turns sporadic exercise into a repeatable weekly pattern.
waypoints.completionCriteria: One week is completed with three 30-minute bodyweight workouts at home, using the available slots.

moves.title: Pick the three workout slots
moves.rationale: Lock in the week before trying to perform it.

moves.title: Do the first 30-minute home workout
moves.rationale: Convert intention into an actual session.

moves.title: Complete the remaining two sessions
moves.rationale: Finish the first repeatable week.

waypoints.title: Hold the routine through a disrupted week
waypoints.rationale: Consistency means returning to the plan when the week is not cleanly organized.
waypoints.completionCriteria: A second week is completed with three workouts despite at least one change in the usual schedule.

moves.title: Keep the same three workout slots unless one needs to move
moves.rationale: Preserve the structure of the routine.

moves.title: Use a shorter start when motivation is low
moves.rationale: Make the session begin even when the week feels off.

moves.title: Finish all three sessions for the week
moves.rationale: Show the routine can survive disruption.

waypoints.title: Work out without needing to reset
waypoints.rationale: The routine is now self-directed rather than something that depends on constant recommitting.
waypoints.completionCriteria: For several weeks in a row, the three weekly workouts happen with little prompting and feel like part of the normal routine.

moves.title: Start each workout from the same simple trigger
moves.rationale: Reduce friction so sessions begin automatically.

moves.title: Repeat the weekly pattern without changing the format every week
moves.rationale: Stabilize the routine instead of rebuilding it.

moves.title: Notice missed sessions quickly and resume at the next slot
moves.rationale: Keep the routine from drifting when life interrupts.

suggestedOneMove.title: Pick the three workout slots
suggestedOneMove.rationale: This is the smallest concrete step toward the first full workout week.

raw.personalizedGuidance: The route stays on routine and consistency, using your three 30-minute home slots as the anchor.

context.intention: I successfully complete my first half marathon.
context.actualStartingPoint: I run 5 km comfortably twice a week. I can train three days each week. I have never completed a half marathon.
context.destinationDescription: I successfully complete my first half marathon.

analysis.startingPointSummary: The person already runs 5 km comfortably twice a week and can train three days per week, but has never completed a half marathon.
assumptions: The destination is the first completed half marathon, not a specific finish time.
No injury, medical, or equipment constraints beyond what was stated.
Current 5 km runs are a stable base to build from without adding extra training days.

routeDesign.complexityReason: This is a first endurance event with a clear endpoint, but it requires several distinct achievements: build a reliable training base, extend long-run endurance, prove the body can handle a longer effort with recovery, and then complete the event.
routeDesign.countReason: Four waypoints fit the distinct progression without turning the route into a distance ladder. Each waypoint marks a real change in readiness, not just a longer run.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: A first long run beyond the current comfortable 5 km that still fits the available three-day training pattern shows the route is moving beyond the starting base.

waypoints.title: Build a reliable long run base
waypoints.rationale: The first change is moving from short comfortable runs to a longer weekly run that the body can handle consistently.
waypoints.completionCriteria: You have completed at least one weekly long run beyond your current 5 km base and can keep the three-day training pattern going for a first full training block.

moves.title: Add one longer run each week
moves.rationale: Make the weekly long run the anchor workout, starting from a distance you can finish with control.

moves.title: Keep the other two runs easy
moves.rationale: Preserve recovery while the long run grows.

moves.title: Record how you feel after each run
moves.rationale: Use the body's response to confirm the new base is holding.

waypoints.title: Extend to a comfortable 10 km long run
waypoints.rationale: A half marathon becomes more realistic once a 10 km run is repeatable without leaving you overly drained.
waypoints.completionCriteria: You can complete a 10 km long run and still recover well enough to continue the next week’s training.

moves.title: Stretch the long run in small steps
moves.rationale: Increase the weekly long run gradually until 10 km is reachable.

moves.title: Hold the easy pace on shorter runs
moves.rationale: Protect energy so the longer run can improve.

moves.title: Use one recovery day after the long run
moves.rationale: Let the body settle before the next training session.

waypoints.title: Finish a strong 15 km effort
waypoints.rationale: This shows you can sustain effort for most of the race distance and recover from it.
waypoints.completionCriteria: You complete a 15 km run with control and return to normal training within the next week.

moves.title: Progress the long run beyond 10 km
moves.rationale: Move into the distance range where race day feels physically familiar.

moves.title: Keep one midweek run steady
moves.rationale: Maintain running rhythm while the long run gets harder.

moves.title: Practice pre-run fuel and hydration
moves.rationale: Learn what supports energy on longer efforts.

waypoints.title: Complete the half marathon
waypoints.rationale: The final state is crossing the finish after covering the full distance.
waypoints.completionCriteria: You start and finish your first half marathon.

moves.title: Taper the week before race day
moves.rationale: Arrive with fresh legs rather than carrying training fatigue.

moves.title: Start at a controlled pace
moves.rationale: Set up the run so the distance is finishable.

moves.title: Keep moving through the final kilometers
moves.rationale: Use the preparation you've built to reach the finish.

suggestedOneMove.title: Add one longer run each week
suggestedOneMove.rationale: This is the smallest concrete step toward the first real change in state.

raw.personalizedGuidance: The route stays focused on endurance readiness and race completion, using your current 5 km base and three training days per week.

context.actualStartingPoint: Anchor is launched with 20 paying users. I am the solo developer, with 10 hours a week for growth and no paid advertising budget. I can contact current users and have subscription analytics.

vision.title: A sustainable Anchor business
vision.description: 10,000 paying users who continue using Anchor

analysis.startingPointSummary: Anchor is already launched with 20 paying users, solo-built, with 10 hours a week for growth, no paid ad budget, and access to current users plus subscription analytics.
assumptions: Current users can be contacted directly for feedback and retention work.
Subscription analytics can show paying-user counts and basic usage patterns.
Growth must come from product retention and repeatable low-cost acquisition, not paid advertising.

routeDesign.complexityReason: This is a multi-stage business growth goal with distinct required outcomes: improve retention, find a repeatable acquisition motion, prove small-scale growth, build a sustainable operating rhythm, and then reach the destination scale.
routeDesign.countReason: Five waypoints cover the dependent achievements without collapsing them into a single scale-up number or adding filler. The current starting point skips launch, so the route begins with retention proof and then moves through repeatability and scale capacity before the final user base.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: A clear retention signal from current paying users, evidenced by a contacted cohort, specific reasons they stay or leave, and one shipped change that improves continued use.

raw.destination: 10,000 paying users who continue using Anchor

waypoints.title: Understand why paying users stay
waypoints.rationale: Retention has to improve before scale makes sense.
waypoints.completionCriteria: You have direct evidence from current paying users about what keeps them subscribed and what makes them drop off.
requirements: Contacted a meaningful sample of current paying users
Collected reasons for continuing and reasons for canceling or lapsing
Identified the top repeat pain point or value driver from the responses
Shipped one change or message that responds to that evidence

moves.title: Message current users for feedback
moves.rationale: Starts the retention evidence collection with people already paying.

moves.title: Review analytics for usage patterns
moves.rationale: Uses the data you already have to see where people are getting value or stalling.

moves.title: Ship one retention-focused adjustment
moves.rationale: Turns the feedback into an observable product or communication change.

waypoints.title: Hold a better first month for new users
waypoints.rationale: A stronger early experience is the foundation for keeping paying users.
waypoints.completionCriteria: New paying users can get to a clear first success and keep using Anchor without extra hand-holding.
requirements: Clear first-use path is in place
At least one onboarding or activation improvement has shipped
New users can reach the core value of Anchor quickly
Early confusion or drop-off points have been reduced in practice

moves.title: Map the first paid-user journey
moves.rationale: Shows where the first-month experience breaks down.

moves.title: Ship the smallest onboarding fix
moves.rationale: Improves the first experience without requiring a larger rebuild.

moves.title: Check recent signups for friction
moves.rationale: Confirms whether the new path is clearer for actual users.

waypoints.title: Find one repeatable acquisition channel
waypoints.rationale: Growth needs a way to bring in new paying users consistently without ads.
waypoints.completionCriteria: You have one acquisition source that reliably produces new paying users through a repeatable process you can run yourself.
requirements: Chosen one acquisition source that fits a solo founder
Repeated the same outreach or content process more than once
Observed new paying users coming from that source
Can explain the steps needed to repeat the channel next week

moves.title: Test one low-cost channel idea
moves.rationale: Finds the first plausible source of new users without budget.

moves.title: Repeat the same outreach or content twice
moves.rationale: Checks whether the source is actually repeatable, not a one-off.

moves.title: Track which contacts convert to paying users
moves.rationale: Separates promising activity from real acquisition results.

waypoints.title: Support steady monthly growth
waypoints.rationale: A repeatable channel has to be able to keep working as volume increases.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Anchor can add paying users regularly while you keep retention work and support load under control.
requirements: Repeatable acquisition is still working after multiple cycles
Support and product maintenance fit within your available time
Retention work is not blocked by acquisition work
You can keep the system going without ad spend

moves.title: Set a weekly growth rhythm
moves.rationale: Keeps acquisition and retention from competing for attention.

moves.title: Handle the next wave of user questions
moves.rationale: Protects the experience as more people arrive.

moves.title: Keep the channel running for several weeks
moves.rationale: Shows the system still works when it is no longer new.

waypoints.title: Reach 10,000 paying users
waypoints.rationale: This is the destination state described in the vision.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Anchor has 10,000 paying users and the business is still supported by retention and repeatable acquisition.

moves.title: Keep improving retention and acquisition together
moves.rationale: The final scale depends on both sides staying healthy.

moves.title: Use the repeatable channel to compound growth
moves.rationale: Continued acquisition is what carries the user base to the destination.

moves.title: Maintain service quality as the user base expands
moves.rationale: Prevents growth from breaking the experience that keeps users paying.

suggestedOneMove.title: Message current users for feedback
suggestedOneMove.rationale: This is the smallest useful step toward the first retention milestone.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Because paid ads are off the table, the route starts with retention evidence and a repeatable low-cost acquisition motion.
